PATHWAY MODULATION: No biomarker data available to assess whether protein degradation pathway was activated downstream of cereblon engagement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (complete response) clearly failed - only 11% CR rate (95% CI: 3-25%) in a single-arm trial. Total response rate was also low at 14%. These response rates are below what would be considered clinically meaningful for AML. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup analysis - median cytogenetic abnormalities were similar between responders and non-responders, suggesting no clear biomarker-defined subset benefited. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm Phase 2 trial with adequate sample size (41 patients) and long duration (260 weeks). High toxicity burden with 40.5% febrile neutropenia, 56.8% grade 3-5 thrombocytopenia, and 43.2% grade 3-5 neutropenia, but the trial was completed and efficacy was assessed. The failure appears to be mechanistic rather than operational.
